title: Pointwise differential criterion for smoothness
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $x\in X$, let $s=f(x)$, and put $d=\dim_x(X_s)$ for the dimension at $x$ [def-kun-dimension] of the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Say that $f$ is smooth at $x$ if there is an open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$ such that $f|_U:U\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $f$ is smooth at $x$ if and only if the local ring map $\mathcal O_{S,s}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and the $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $\Omega^1_{X/S,x}$, the stalk of the relative differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], can be generated by at most $d$ elements.

source.place: Tag 01V9 (morphisms-lemma-smooth-at-point), equivalence of (1) and (3); 'smooth at x' as in Morphisms Definition 01V5

mathlib_searches.query: For a locally finitely presented morphism, smoothness at a point is equivalent to flatness and relative differentials generated by at most fibre dimension
mathlib_searches.results: AlgebraicGeometry.isSmoothOfRelativeDimension_iff and AlgebraicGeometry.isSmooth_iff; no pointwise differential-generator criterion.
5 generic smooth/formally-unramified API hits in Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry; no criterion using fibre dimension and differential generators.
